feat(orchestration): add the loopback-only remote Host orchestration plane

Stage D of chapter 18 was delivered design-first. The design lands in the
chapter itself: §7 records the entities, their owning domains, their
lifetimes and the authoritative fact source — an orchestration operation is
process-local and never persisted, and it is not the remote installer's own
operation record — then the four REST endpoints and their payload;
§8 the state machine, idempotency, cancellation and audit; §9 the local
source and outbound target policy.

The Host runs every SSH action. SshCommandLine is the single argv authority:
the target carries a host plus optional user, port and identity path, an
absent field adds no option, the identity travels as a path for `-i`, and the
user's own ~/.ssh/config supplies whatever the request omits. The Host-owned
`ssh-known-hosts` is written with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes only after the
user compares the scanned fingerprint, so a first connection establishes no
session and sends nothing; a changed fingerprint fails with a structured
error instead. RemoteOrchestration reuses RemoteHostInstaller for the
install steps rather than starting a second installer, and reclaims every
child process, tunnel included, when an operation is cancelled or times out.
Failures become stable codes with parameters; the Host produces no
user-facing copy, keeps no credential in any audit event, and the entry
refuses anything that is not a loopback subject sending a marked non-simple
request. The HCP capability set stays closed, which a descriptor test now
asserts.

The web panel submits structured fields, shows progress as a projection,
asks for the fingerprint before the first connection, and offers cancel while
the operation is waiting or running. Verified with 188 Java tests, 204 web
tests, the production build, and a real browser at 1440x900, 820x900 and
412x915 in both themes and both locales.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
